name: Women Who Wrote the World: Novelists, Poets and Diarists
description: From a Heian court lady to Toni Morrison and J. K. Rowling: the women whose books, often written under pen names or against the odds, changed literature.

checkpoints.name: A story from the court
checkpoints.note: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady at the Japanese court, writes The Tale of Genji around 1010, a long story of love and court life that is often counted among the first novels ever written. In the centuries that follow, women who publish fiction remain rare, though writers such as Madame de La Fayette and Aphra Behn find readers in the 1600s.

checkpoints.name: Pens and pen names
checkpoints.note: Mary Wollstonecraft argues in 1792, in A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, that girls deserve a real education. Jane Austen publishes Pride and Prejudice in 1813, Mary Shelley's Frankenstein appears in 1818, and Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre follows in 1847 under the pen name Currer Bell.

checkpoints.name: Novels with causes
checkpoints.note: Harriet Beecher Stowe's Uncle Tom's Cabin (1852) turns many readers against slavery. George Eliot, the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, writes searching realist novels, and Louisa May Alcott draws on her own family for her stories. Emily Dickinson writes a vast body of poems, only a few printed in her lifetime.

checkpoints.name: Rooms of their own
checkpoints.note: Virginia Woolf experiments with how a novel can show a mind at work. Agatha Christie's Murder on the Orient Express (1934) and And Then There Were None (1939) sell in huge numbers and shape the detective story. Anne Frank's diary, written in hiding, is published in 1947 and becomes one of the most read books of the century.

checkpoints.name: Prizes and bestsellers
checkpoints.note: Maya Angelou tells her life in a series of memoirs, and Toni Morrison and Wisława Szymborska win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993 and 1996. Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale (1985) imagines a harsh religious state, and J. K. Rowling's Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (1997) begins a series read by millions.
